$description: UberTib responsive thresholds. TWO DISTINCT SETS that must never be merged. Profile C has size classes on a device viewport with no media queries available; Profile A has a conceptual content grid measured on the panel content area, which is the viewport minus a framework-owned shell whose width this chain does not control. A single shared scale would be wrong for both: a 1024px viewport on Profile A is not a 1024px content area. The literal thresholds live under primitive; the profile groups name them.

threshold.$description: Every responsive threshold in the product. Two scales, deliberately kept apart even though two values coincide.

verification-width.$description: The narrow widths every Patient surface is checked against for horizontal overflow. 280 is the smallest supported device width and is the one that actually finds bugs.

profile-c.$description: Patient app, React Native. Size classes, not media queries. One primary reading column at every class; a wider class may place tightly related comparison values side by side, but task order stays identical. Phase 2 fixed this and it is not reopened here.

compact.$description: Phones in portrait. The design target.

medium.$description: Large phones in landscape and small tablets. The reading column widens to its measure ceiling and stops.

expanded.$description: Tablets. Still one primary reading column, centred, capped at its measure ceiling. Not a two-pane layout.

reading-column-max.$description: In characters, not pixels. The column stops growing at its measure ceiling however wide the device is; whitespace takes the remainder.

stack-threshold.$description: Not a width. At the largest supported text size, critical regions STACK rather than truncate or scroll sideways, at every size class. Truncating an amount, a deadline or a controlling reason is a correctness failure, not a layout compromise.

profile-a.$description: Clinic and Admin Filament panels. A twelve-column conceptual content grid inside a framework-owned shell. Thresholds are measured on the CONTENT AREA width, not the viewport, because the shell navigation width is framework-owned and can change without this chain being consulted.

narrow.$description: Tablet, or desktop with the shell navigation expanded over a small viewport. Twelve columns collapse to one; a supporting rail moves below the primary content.

medium.$description: Two-region layouts resolve: primary content plus a supporting rail.

wide.$description: The working default. Full twelve-column behaviour.

maximum.$description: Content stops widening here. Beyond it the extra width becomes margin, because a table row wider than this loses the association between its first and its last cell.

tablet-note.$description: PO-UX-07 confirms tablet as a secondary but genuine context for the clinic representative, invited staff and the treating dentist. A narrow content width is therefore a supported layout rather than a degraded one, and the dense mode may not assume a mouse.
